answer: Sybil resistance works by making every agent identity pay the same verifiable cost a real participant pays. Each agent binds to one human anchor and locks a bonded stake before bidding. Cloning a thousand puppets means locking a deposit per clone, and collusion slashes them, so fleet cost is deposit times count, far above honest reach. The registry acts like a pigment that marks duplicates instantly, and a sybil at the vertex of a fake cluster collapses it once one stake is forfeited. Every forged identity in that orchard carries skin in the game, so a large fleet costs more than it earns.
